learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems of simple analog electronic circuits.
Ability to prepare a technical report on electronics work including a calculation part and an experimental part.
Ability to explain the differences between the characteristics of different logic families and relate them to each other.
Ability to explain the physical principle of semiconductors and the operation of basic analog electronic components.
Ability to explain the operation of basic digital electronic components.
Ability to describe the most common analog application circuits.
Ability to calculate simple analog electronic circuits and analyze their behavior.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of voltage and current amplifiers.
Semiconductor diode. Analysis and design of circuits with diodes.
The bipolar junction transistor. Analysis and design of BJT circuits.
The field-effect transistor. Analysis and design of FET circuits.
Principle of operation of field-effect transistors.
Basic equation in the active region.
Discrete 4-layer devices: thyristors, diacs, triacs, GTO.
Operational amplifiers. Analysis and design of operational amplifier circuits.
Power amplifiers and power supplies. Analysis and design.
Class B and Class AB amplifiers.
Combinational logic. Truth tables and logic functions.
teaching_methods: Lectures: Expository method consisting of presenting a logically structured topic to provide organized information. Primarily focused on verbal exposition by the professor, supported by multimedia techniques.

Problem-solving by the professor: The professor develops and interprets solutions by applying routines, formulas, or procedures to transform initially proposed information. Used as a complement to the lecture.

Problem-solving by the student: Situations where the student must develop and interpret appropriate solutions by applying routines, formulas, or procedures to transform initially proposed information.

Laboratory work: Method consisting of students developing specific scientific-technological laboratory work under the professor's supervision. This methodology is characterized by the high autonomy with which students must work.

Learning through the Virtual Classroom: Teaching-learning situation using a computer with network connection as a communication system between professor-student, developing a plan of formative activities integrated into the curriculum.
assessment_rules: The student will pass the course if they obtain a minimum of 5 out of 10 points in the global average grade. To pass, a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required in the final exam, in addition to a global grade of 5 or higher. If the minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is not achieved in the final exam, the course grade will be that of the final exam. Continuous assessment grades are valid only for the two calls of the current academic year, and laboratory practices cannot be recovered. For extraordinary calls, the final exam accounts for 100% of the grade.
